target_customer: Medium sized businesses on AWS with 50 to 100 servers and a small ops team, later IT operations and DevOps teams
problem: On call engineers are woken by alerts for routine problems. Neptune.io ran automated fix scripts and enriched alerts so incidents resolved faster.

founders.name: Kiran Gollu
prior_employers: Rubrik (Head of Cloud Platform Engineering, per YC founder page)
Amazon Web Services (founding engineer on S3 and DynamoDB, per YC founder page; five years at AWS per TechCrunch 2014-08-15)

founders.name: Satish Talluri
founders.background_notes: Per YC founder page; later a partner on the infrastructure investing team at a16z.

exit.reason: No shutdown or acquisition notice found. YC lists the company as inactive and the domain now hosts an unrelated blockchain project.

competitors.name: New Relic
competitors.what: Application monitoring that detects problems, with more basic scripting than Neptune.io

competitors.name: PagerDuty
competitors.what: Alerting and on call routing, sits next to Neptune.io's position between monitoring and alerting

technical_complexity.rationale: Integrating with monitoring tools and running remediation scripts safely on customer servers is standard but sensitive engineering. The founders had AWS operations experience.

defensibility.rationale: Runbook libraries could lock in customers over time, but monitoring and alerting vendors could add scripted responses.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Later incident response tools such as StackPulse and incident.io emerged. No source shows an incumbent buying Neptune.io.

market_need_then: TechCrunch (2014-08-15) describes on call admins woken for routine issues and notes large firms like Netflix, Google and Facebook built similar auto fix scripts in house. The company had paying pilot customers by August 2014.

branding.domain_note: Used neptune.io, a .io domain. The domain now hosts Neptune Privacy, an unrelated blockchain project.

identity.voice_and_tone: Engineer to engineer, focused on saving sleep for on call staff

branding.community_and_virality: Presented on StackShare. No community or merch found.

brand_strength.rationale: A pleasant name but confusable with Neptune.ai (ML tooling, acquired by OpenAI per 2025 reports) and other Neptunes, which muddies search.

outcome_analysis: Neptune.io built automated fixes for server alerts, was self funded before YC Summer 2014 and showed paying pilots, and aggregators report a seed of about one million dollars. YC lists it as inactive, and its CEO later started Oodle.ai in 2023, but no document explains why or when Neptune.io stopped, so the cause is not public and failure factors stay empty. Crowded monitoring and alerting vendors were the obvious squeeze.
notes: Seed of about 1M with Y Combinator rests on aggregators only (CB Insights lists Aug 16, 2014; StartupIntros Nov 1, 2014; Village total 1M), so only the year is recorded. TechCrunch says the company was self financed and planned formal fundraising in the fall of 2014. StartupIntros also lists a Series A of about 8M in March 2022 under Neptune.io, which looks like a conflation with a different Neptune company and is not recorded. Founder education not found. Talluri is described as a founder on the YC page; TechCrunch calls him a co-founder.
